title: Finland Work Visa Requirements 2026: Complete Guide
metaDescription: Finland work visa requirements 2026: job offer rules, Migri residence permit types, documents, fees, processing steps and the path to permanent residence.
headline: Finland Work Visa Requirements 2026: Complete Guide

sections.title: What is the Finland work visa route?
sections.content:
Finland does not have a single generic work visa: most workers apply for a residence permit for an employed person, based on a specific job offer from a Finnish employer. The permit is tied to that employer and role at first, and the employer must meet Finnish employment and pay standards before the permit can be granted.

Applications are handled by the Finnish Immigration Service, known as Migri, usually through its Enter Finland online service, followed by an appointment at a Finnish mission abroad to prove identity. Processing times vary by permit type and season, so apply well before your planned start date.

sections.title: Requirements for workers and employers
sections.content:
Workers generally need a signed employment contract or binding job offer, a valid passport, and enough income to support themselves in Finland. The employer must confirm the terms, working hours and pay, and for many roles the Employment and Economic Development Office checks that labour market conditions are met.

Some categories are simpler: specialists, researchers, startup founders and seasonal workers have their own permit types with different income and documentation rules. Check the Migri page for your exact category, because using the wrong permit type is a common reason for delays or refusals.

sections.title: Documents, fees and processing
sections.content:
Typical documents include a passport, employment contract, salary and working-hours details, and sometimes degree certificates, work references or proof of accommodation. Migri publishes the current fee for each permit type, and fees are paid online when the application is submitted.

After submitting online, book an identification appointment promptly, because the processing clock often depends on that visit. Keep your contact details up to date in Enter Finland, and respond quickly to any request for additional documents, since unanswered requests can lead to a negative decision.

sections.title: After arrival and longer-term stay
sections.content:
Once the permit is granted, register your residence, obtain a Finnish personal identity code if you do not already have one, and open the practical steps for work, housing and healthcare in your municipality. Your employer should help with the first payroll, tax card and occupational healthcare arrangements.

After several years of continuous legal residence and work in Finland, many permit holders can apply for a permanent residence permit or an extended permit, subject to income, residence and language or integration requirements in force at the time. Plan early, because gaps in employment or residence can affect eligibility.

faqs.q: Do you need a job offer for a Finland work permit?
faqs.a: Yes, most Finland work-based residence permits require a specific job offer or signed employment contract from a Finnish employer before you apply. The employer must confirm the pay, hours and terms, and for many roles the authorities also check labour market conditions before granting the permit.

faqs.q: How do you apply for a Finland work residence permit?
faqs.a: You usually apply online through Migri's Enter Finland service, pay the current fee, and then attend an identification appointment at a Finnish mission abroad. Processing times vary by permit type, so submit early, keep documents complete, and respond quickly to any request for more evidence.

faqs.q: Which Finland permit type should you choose?
faqs.a: The right type depends on your role: employed persons, specialists, researchers, startup founders and seasonal workers each have different permits and income rules. Check the Migri page for your exact category before applying, because choosing the wrong permit type is a common cause of delay or refusal.

faqs.q: Can a Finland work permit lead to permanent residence?
faqs.a: After several years of continuous legal residence and work in Finland, many permit holders can apply for a permanent residence permit or an extended permit. Eligibility depends on income, continuous residence and any language or integration requirements in force at that time, so keep employment and residence records complete.
